INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE MAY 3, 2021
  OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT MEETING

The Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District meeting will be closed to the public in
compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-
19 Virus. Additionally, the meeting will be conducted via teleconference with members
participating remotely. Considering this, the customary meeting format has been modified.
Even with this change in format, the City is still encouraging public participation and wishes to
make residents aware of the following opportunities for participation:

  1) View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream

  2) Please submit your written comments via email at planning@cityoflaverne.org. They
  will be shared with the District Board Members prior to the meeting and will be made
  part of the permanent record. We ask that you provide those emails before 7:00 p.m.
  the day before the meeting. Please be advised that public comments submitted by
  emails or any other format to the City are public records that will be made
  available for public viewing.

  3) For individuals that wish to share their comments during the live stream, you may
  email planning@cityoflaverne.org by 7:00 a.m. on the day of the meeting with a phone
  number and the item(s) you wish to speak on. We will call you back at the appropriate
  time during the meeting for your comment.

  4) Additionally, if you wish to participate via Zoom, you will need to register before 8:00
  a.m. on the date of the meeting and please be aware that space is limited.

  https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_UTD1RqXaRX2tNWeeOsaTYg

  You will be provided a link after registering and will have the ability to watch the
  meeting live. If you wish to speak during the meeting, you can “raise your hand” as
  appropriate on the current agenda item(s). Once it is your turn to speak, you will be
  brought into the meeting and have the ability to speak and turn on your video when
  called upon.

  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, April 5, 2021

1.  The teleconference meeting was called to order by Chairperson Craig Walters at 8:35a.m.
  Mr. Walters stated that questions can be emailed to planning@cityoflaverne.org.

  Advisory Board Members present: Craig Walters, Jason Miller, and Matt Forgey.
  Absent: Marianne Stark and Micky Rehm. City Representatives present: Community
  Development Director Eric Scherer. Others present: Sean Franco.

2.  CALENDAR

  Cool Cruise – Saturday, September 11, 2021
  Cruisin La Verne – Saturday, November 20, 2021

3.  APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES February 1, 2021 and March 1, 2021

  It was moved by Mr. Miller and seconded by Mr. Forgey to approve the minutes as
  submitted. Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

4.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Proposed for La Verne Cool Cruise – Saturday, September 11, 2021
  Mr. Scherer state that two dates were presented to Mr. Hoelzel for the event and
  he chose Saturday, September 11th.

  One public comment was received via email.

  It was moved by Mr. Miller and seconded by Mr. Forgey to support the date.
  Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

  B.  Proposed Budget – Recommendation to the City Council
  Mr. Scherer previously met with Ms. Rehm and Mr. Walters to discuss the budget
  and make adjustments.

  One public comment was received via email.

  It was moved by Mr. Miller and seconded by Mr. Forgey to recommend approval
  of the proposed budget to City Council. Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  D Street Closure - Mr. Scherer stated that he was made aware of a potential
  petition to re-open the street. The Board discussed the timing for opening D
  Street. Mr. Scherer stated that he would continue to look at expanded outdoor
  1
   dining. It was decided that a decision when to re-open the street was not needed at
  this time.

  B.  Alternate Board Member Interest – Mr. Scherer indicated that there was one
  person who continued to be interested in serving on the Board, and introduced
  new co-owner of Chase’s, Sean Franco. Mr. Franco gave a brief introduction and
  stated why he was interested in serving on the Board.

  It was moved by Mr. Miller and seconded by Mr. Forgey to recommend to the
  City Council to appoint Sean Franco to alternate member and appoint Matt
  Forgey as a regular member. Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A.  City Report (Eric Scherer): None
  B.  University Report (Jason Miller): Mr. Miller stated that there will be a phased
  return for staff.
  C.  Marketing (Micky Rehm): None
  D.  Chamber Report (Leah Skinner): None
  E.  Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): None
  F.  Financial Report: None

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

  No public comments were received.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  Meeting was adjourned at 9:18 a.m., to the next meeting to be held on Monday, May 3,
  2021 at 8:30 a.m.

  Respectively submitted,

  _____________________
  Natalie M. Hiatt

 City Email Sent April 15, 2021:

Hi D Street Restaurant Owners:

In light of the Governor’s announcement that his plan is to fully re-open the State on June 15th, we have
been discussing the closure of D Street. This week, a letter (attached) was delivered to me from some
business owners calling for the street to be reopened now.

There was also a discussion at the last BID Board meeting on April 5th about D street and that perhaps
there could still be expanded outdoor seating in the parking spaces in front of your business and allow
the street to reopen. In this scenario, the businesses would be responsible in building out the spaces to
be a bit more permanent (as is seen in the Claremont Village) with a commitment by the City to allow
them to remain for a while.

I have also reached out to ABC to determine if they will be revoking the temporary permits many of you
received in order to expand your serving areas. While they haven’t made a decision, they indicated that
businesses would be provided at least 30 day notice prior to them changing any of the rules that they
put in place with Covid.

Also keep in mind that if the State reopens everything on June 15th, the County of LA would also need to
do the same, and as you know, their track record has been to be more restrictive than the State.
However, there has been some indication that the County would follow the State on this, provided the
numbers are stable and there is not another spike.

Basically, we really need to know what your plans are with the use of D Street. With the 50% inside
occupancy allowance, do you still have a need or want to continue the expanded outdoor seating? If so,
do you want to continue it in this configuration or would be willing to reduce it to the parking spaces in
order to open the street? Do you want to do this now or wait for June 15th? Would you continue to
want to use the area if ABC does revoke your permits to serve out there?

The City Council will have to make a decision on how to move forward, but your input is vital in allowing
them to do so. It is extremely important to let us know what your thoughts are on this issue.

Please email or call me with your thoughts.

Thanks.

Eric Scherer, AICP
Community Development Director
City of La Verne
3660 D Street
La Verne, CA 91750
Office: 909-596-8706
escherer@cityoflaverne.org
   RESPONSES RECEIVED AS OF APRIL 29, 2021

Spooners:

Mr. Scherer,

Thank you for your email. I’m on the fence with D street remaining closed.
Of course the street closure helped all the restaurants tremendously during the lock down and I am
forever grateful for what the city has done for us restaurant owners. However, I noticed more trash all
over the street, public drunkenness, customers complaining of no parking space, and with sports games
played in the canopy by other venues, my customers have experience not so pleasant time while they
dined outside. Again goes back to public drunkenness and unruly crowd at nights.
Dealing with weekend melees of people partying outside has been a struggle.
As much as I love the set up right now, I’m beginning to doubt if it’s even worth it. My husband is all for
keeping the street closed and remain the way it is but he’s not the one working here everyday to
experience the bad side of it.
If the D street remains the way it is now, I would like to ask that we have more rules and policies for the
restaurants to follow to keep our street clean and safe.

Roberta’s Village Inn:

Hi Eric,

First I want to say Thank You for all you and the City have done for us.
We would like the Outdoor Dining to remain the same until at least June 15th. We aren't interested in
taking away our parking spaces once the Street reopens.
Hopefully we can still use the Sidewalk as extra dining space.

Roberta’s Village Inn Second Email:

I would like to begin by thanking the City of La Verne and the other business owners of D street for
approving the street closure during these tough times. We appreciate the overwhelming positivity and
support you have shown in protecting our small businesses during this pandemic.This street closure has
benefited us greatly and has saved our small business which would otherwise close because of the
pandemic.We have heard an overwhelming amount of positive comments about our outdoor seating
arrangements. Numerous customers commend the city for allowing us this type of arrangement. Some
customers even suggested that this closure be made permanent. However I as a business owner
understand that this arrangement does not work for all the businesses on D st. I would like to ask that
the street closure be kept up until we are at 100% capacity inside and would prefer that it remain as it is
now. As far as using the parking spaces I think that there is a little more liability and it is not as enjoyable
with the noise of the cars so for now I will pass on that.Once again thank you to the city of la Verne for
providing us with this amazing opportunity for outdoor seating

Café Wang:

Hi Eric,

Thank you for the update regarding the future of D Street.

In answer to your specific questions:
 1. We would like to continue expanded outdoor dining and would be willing to reduce the area to the
parking spaces. There undoubtedly will be customers who would prefer to sit outdoors, for
precautionary reasons, even after the pandemic is officially over.

2. We want to work collectively with all the businesses who have been affected with the th D St.
closure. And we support opening D St asap in order to help non-restaurant businesses get back to
normal. Indeed, it has been a struggle just to survive for nearly all small businesses owners.

3. We would still like the outdoor accomodation whether or not ABC revokes permits.

If possible, we would like to continue to use the parking lot areas in front of the restaurant and dessert
shop on a long term basis. With the commitment of the City, we would seek to construct permanant
structures to accommodate outdoor dining, alongside a D St. that is open to traffic.

We believe that the La Verne Old Town District has the potential in a very short time to be something
even more special than it already is. Following in the footsteps of Claremont Village would help create a
similar ambiance that the area that it is well known for. And with the reopening of the University, in a
few months, and the Gold Line in a couple years, it is predictable that the district will become a focal
point within the City, with students, locals and tourists alike coming to see how much Old Town has
transformed.

Allowing all the restaurants in the district to increase its outdoor dining footprint will give the
community a greater dining experience. But this is especially true of Cafe Wang, because of all the full
service restaurants in Old Town, Cafe Wang has the smallest outdoor dining area. We believe the
opportunity to expand on a permanent basis would be a "win-win-win" between for the community, the
restaurant and the City.

We want to thank you, as well as the Mayor and the City Council for your consideration. We know that
you must all consider a multitude of factors before coming to a decision that meets your most important
priorities. We thank you for the opportunity to share our input.

House of Wings:

Hi Eric!
So sorry for the delayed response. Thank you for reaching out and allowing us to give an input on the
outdoor seating decision.
We highly prioritize and appreciate D St. being closed as it has allowed us ample seating. Our customers
have been extremely vocal about the seating situation and many have expressed that they (1) enjoy that
they have the option to sit indoor or outdoor and (2) many have voiced that they hope D St. stays closed
at least through the warm summer months because they'd like to continue sitting outside.

Both our employees and customers appear to feel safer outside. There were concerns about people
driving by the smaller seating sections on D St. as closing off a few parking spaces would make for a
narrow lane. We are not sure if our customers would be interested in sitting in an area so close to motor
traffic. Of course, if the option was parking space seating or nothing, we would take what we could get.
We hope to continue to have the option for tent seating but understand the situation the city is in when
it comes to making this business decision.
 Lordsburg:

Eric,
I have been circulating this letter to our patrons for a couple of weeks. We probably have 100+
signatures of local residents.
